title.narrative: Capacity for Transparency-UNDP-ARM-00109279

description.narrative: Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency project will provide support for building institutional and technical capacities to meet enhanced transparency requirements as defined in Article 13 of the Paris Agreement.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

title.narrative: Annual Output Results
Output Indicator

description.narrative: Mandatory Indicator 1: # direct project beneficiaries disaggregated by gender (individual people) CBIT Core Indicator 2: Quality of MRV Systems CBIT Core Indicator 3 Institutional Capacity for Transparency-Related Activities 4: Presence of institutional arrangements for a national transparency framework 5: Presence of legal and/or regulatory requirements for a national transparency framework 6: Presence of an operational MRV system that is being used for continuous data collection and reporting to the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement with gender disaggregated data where relevant 7: Use of sectoral templates for GHG data collection in key sectors of the inventory 8: Number of sub-sectors where emissions estimates are more robust. 9: Use of standardized methodologies and guidelines in transparency reporting. 10: Coverage of gender issues in climate change reporting 11: Armenia is able to track its progress towards its NDCs 12: Accessibility of information regarding transparency initiatives and climate change reporting in Armenia. 13: Consideration of gender issues in progress towards the NDC

comment.narrative: 1. 0 2. 5 3. 2 4. There are currently no formal institutional arrangements for a national transparency framework. 5. Data sharing for reporting on climate change among different institutions is currently done on an informal, voluntary basis. 6. Data are currently collected on an ad hoc, project-by-project basis 7. Different approaches are used for data collected by different entities. 8. Certain discrepancies in sub-sector data exist, particularly in the AFOLU sector. 9. No common methodology is used for assessing and reporting on mitigation policies and actions, support received, and adaptation to climate change. 10. Gender and climate change issues are not mentioned in national climate change documents such as the NCs and BURs 11. No tracking system or report exists for NDCs. 12. Climate change reports from Armenia are available in different locations on the Internet. Information on transparency initiatives in Armenia is partially available in different locations. 13. Gender and climate change issues are not mentioned in the current NDC.

1. Draft Government Decree on approval of the process of organizing collection of data and information necessary for the development of the National GHG Inventory reports under UNFCCC developed 2. Climate change introductory trainings for the Interagency Climate Change Council and its working groups conducted 3. Technical specifications of climate change MRV platform developed 4. Activities under LOA with the Hydrometeorology and Monitoring Center SNCO envisaged for 2022 implemented 5. Sectoral templates on data collection and reporting for the GHG inventory developed 6. Data collection protocol on mitigation policies and measures and their effects in Armenia developed

1. Draft Government Decree on approval of the process of organizing collection of data and information necessary for the development of the National GHG Inventory reports under UNFCCC was developed 2. Climate change introductory trainings for the Interagency Climate Change Council and its working groups were delivered 3. The development of technical specifications of climate change MRV platform is in the process (the delay is due to the fact that the amendments to Law on Atmospheric Air Protection which will establish an obligation to provide the GHG data on regular basis were adopted in December 2022). 4. Activities under LOA with the Hydrometeorology and Monitoring Center SNCO envisaged for 2022 were implemented 5. Sectoral templates on data collection and reporting for the GHG inventory were developed. 6. The development of data collection protocol on mitigation policies and measures and their effects in Armenia is in process (will be finalized in January 2023).

1. Inception phase arrangements done Inception report submitted 2. Preliminary arrangements on National institutional arrangements for an enhanced transparency framework (ETF) drafted 3. Preliminary arrangements on MRV systems in support of an ETF drafted 4,. Preliminary arrangements on Capacity building to support transparency-related activities over time drafted 5. Monitoring and Evaluation and Knowledge Management conducted 6.. Ongoing Project Management ensured
